title: Briefing: Germany, Albania, Italy, India, Serbia and France
script: Good morning. It's Monday, November second, and this is the Unowned briefing: the stories that matter, checked and graded. It's read by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our published timelines.
Every item carries our grade. Confirmed means independent outlets agree. Reported means one source so far. Disputed means the accounts conflict. And alleged is one side's claim.
Here are the top stories.
Germany. Today: new developments in Germany's Gen Z protests.
Albania. Today: new developments in Albania's student protests.
Italy. Yesterday: new developments in Italy's student and cost-of-living protests.
India. Yesterday: new developments in the Cockroach Janta Party movement.
Serbia. Yesterday: new developments in Serbia's student movement.
France. On Saturday: new developments in France's high school protests.
Canada. No new developments since Friday, October thirtieth.
South Africa. No new developments since Friday, October thirtieth.
Now the details.

Germany. Today: Germany's Education Minister Karin Prien calls the concerns of the young people who marched in more than 30 cities on October thirty-first "legitimate and extremely relevant" and promises more dialogue, and SPD politicians call for a national education summit; these are proposals, not policy changes so far, The Local reports. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, The Local Germany, and isn't yet confirmed by a second. Coming up: Gen Z regelt plans another countrywide protest on November fourteenth.

Albania. Today: Tirana Mayor Erion Veliaj, held in pre-trial detention on corruption charges he denies, accused Prime Minister Edi Rama of orchestrating his October twenty-eighth transfer to Fier prison and of using Justice Minister Toni Gogu to demand he give up control of the city, Tirana Times reports; the claims, relayed in part by his lawyer, are unverified. Gogu said he visited only to check detention conditions and called the allegations fabricated, while the prisons directorate has cited security reasons for the transfer. We grade that disputed: the accounts conflict, and our timeline sets out both.

Italy. Yesterday, Sunday, November first: The education branch of the CGIL union says it will join the CGIL general strike on November twentieth, citing budget-law cuts of 4,925 teaching posts and 2,049 support staff from 2027/28 and no funds for the contract renewal, Scuola Mag reports. These are the union's claims; no government response was in the report. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, Scuola Mag, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.

India. Yesterday, Sunday, November first: Thousands march in New Delhi to Ramlila Maidan in a Congress-led opposition rally, headed by Rahul Gandhi, demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign over a voter-list revision that removed more than 130 million names, Al Jazeera and Reuters report. P. We grade that reported: so far only Al Jazeera has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation.

Serbia. Yesterday, Sunday, November first: Thousands mark two years since the Novi Sad railway station canopy collapse that killed 16 people, with a silent march in the rain, 16 wreaths and 16 minutes of silence, AP and AFP report; students say they now want those responsible to be punished. Our grade: confirmed, with independent reporting from AP and Malay Mail. Also yesterday: Prosecutors order the 48-hour detention of Marko Kričak, head of the criminal police, and another senior officer on suspicion of abuse of office linked to a murder investigation, AP reports. We grade that alleged: it's one side's claim, not independently confirmed. Coming up: Formation of the new government and the choice of prime minister.

France. On Saturday, October thirty-first: More than 300,000 people join a new wave of protests on Saturday, smaller than the mid-October unrest, Bloomberg reports; in Paris, where about 70,000 officers were deployed, police arrest 779 people and five officers are injured. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez calls a Molotov cocktail attack on an officer "attempted murder", and an investigation has been opened, according to AFP. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, Bloomberg, and isn't yet confirmed by a second. Also on Saturday: Student unions call for school blockades this week and urge students to join the cross-sector strike on November fifth, Bloomberg reports. We grade that reported: so far only Bloomberg has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation.
Also on our watch, with no new developments in the last three days.

Canada. The latest report, from Friday, October thirtieth: Tsartlip First Nation, on Vancouver Island, files for judicial review in the Federal Court of the Pacific Link national-interest designation, saying federal consultation was rushed and ignored its treaty rights, CTV News reports. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, CTV News, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.

South Africa. The latest report, from Friday, October thirtieth: A Durban court lets the anti-migrant group March and March keep demonstrating but only between 9am and 3pm, without weapons or face coverings and without damaging property, AFP reports. We grade that reported: so far only 24 News HD has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation.
We'll bring you updates on those as soon as they become available.
Coming up in the days ahead. Wednesday, November fourth, South Africa: Local government elections on November fourth.
That's the Unowned briefing for Monday, November second. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com. Thanks for listening.
